messages.subject: eQTLs
parts: Hello to all, I'm doing an eQTL analysis in my lab, to do so I have the phenotype for 2745 "traits" in my case etraits, I have generated independent QTL for each one, but my boss want a picture that shows every trait at once. I have in mind a picture like this "http://www.rqtl.org/graphs/plot.scantwo.html", but even when it has a tutorial, I'm unable to produce my own picture. If you could guide me I will be thankful

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] eQTLs
parts:
What I've typically done is take the single largest LOD score on each chromosome for each trait, for those peaks with LOD > some threshold. I'd then do a scatterplot of the genomic position of the transcript vs the QTL position.

You might take a look at the neqtl package, which includes these sorts of plots.
Install it as follows:

install.packages(devtools)
library(devtools)
install_github("atbroman/neqtl")

It includes a vignette, which you may view by typing:

vignette("neqtl_intro")

regards,
karl

messages.subject: Re: eQTLs
parts:
Hi, I'm follow your advise and try this:

[CODE]
library(qtl)
library(devtools)
library(neqtl)
pheno <- read.cross("csv", "", "diff_out_noviembre_L3.csv", na.strings="-", genotypes=c("AA", "BB", "AB", "C", "D"), alleles =c("A", "B"))
pheno <- calc.genoprob(pheno, step=1, error.prob=0.001)
scan.f2 <- scanone(pheno,pheno.col=1:100, method="em")
Error in checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  : 
  Following phenotypes are not numeric: Column 1
In addition: There were 34 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
[/CODE]

I revised the file "diff_out_noviembre_L3.csv" and the first column is indeed a numeric one, What am i doing wrong?, thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] eQTLs
parts:
It seems that the first phenotype *isn't* numeric.

Try

sapply(pheno$pheno, is.numeric)

There might be a character string lurking in there that is causing the problem.

karl
